excerpts.capturedContext:
inking of this I have grief and pain at heart, And all night long can find no quietness. It is hard to dwell long in prosperity; Rise and decline cannot be reckoned on. What were formerly lotus buds in May, Now in the autumn are but withered seed-pods. A heavy frost stiffens the prairie grasses- - They wilt despondently and do not quickly die.- The sun and moon come ever circling back. Once we depart we do not shine again. I ponder deeply on times long past and gone Though to remember them tears my very entrails.
